title: Explicit common intersection word and its shrinking triangle
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring, h:X→Z a scheme map, c a compactification of h, H a proper/open/proper presentation, and S=H.shrink(a′,v,fac) as in [def-pur-etale-graph-neighborhood-words]. Put T=H.P×_Z c.Z, O1=T×_(c.Z)X, O2=T×_(H.P)H.U, and I=O1×_T O2 with projections u1,u2. The literal graph s12:X→I is proper. Write w=u1 b1=u2 b2 and P_I=Rs12_* ⋙ Dw_! ⋙ Rq_*, where q:T→Z is the fixed ambient proper map. Define L1:O1_word→P_I as the inverse first proper/open triangle, followed by the inverse open compositor, all under Rq_*. Define L2:P_I→O2_word using the pullback equality w=u2 b2, the second open compositor, and the second proper/open triangle, all under Rq_*. Then graphMiddle.hom=L1.hom≫L2.hom by expansion. For S, construct d:I_S→I_H as pullback.lift(u1_S,u2_S≫graphNeighborhoodShrink). It is an open immersion, commutes with both projections, and s12_S d=s12_H. Its inverse proper/open triangle and open compositor define K:P_I_H≅P_I_S. These are actual pullback maps and specified isomorphism words, with no existence choice.

proof.text: Construct d by the pullback lift. Pullback cancellation identifies its square over the second projection as a base change of graphNeighborhoodShrink, so d is open. The projection equations, graphFirstLift_shrink and graphNeighborhoodShrink_graph prove s12_S d=s12_H. The first projection proves d w_H=w_S. Form K from the inverse proper/open triangle for this equation followed by the open compositor and equality comparison.
